records.title: Quantum PCP: a constant promise gap for local Hamiltonians
records.formal: Are there constants $k$ and $\varepsilon>0$ for which the following promise problem is QMA-hard? The input is $H=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m H_i$ on $n$ qubits, with each term acting on at most $k$ qubits and $0\preceq H_i\preceq I$. Distinguish $\lambda_{\min}(H)\le a$ from $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge b$, promised $b-a\ge\varepsilon$. The reduction must be efficient. This is the normalized Hamiltonian formulation.

records.formal: Is $\mathrm{QMA}=\mathrm{QCMA}$? Both classes have a polynomial-time quantum verifier and bounded error. QMA permits a polynomial-size quantum witness; QCMA permits only a polynomial-length classical string. The question concerns the standard classes without an oracle.

records.title: Can circle–segment reporting on connected planar graphs have additive output cost?
records.formal: Is there a deterministic static data structure that preprocesses a connected straight-line planar graph with n >= 2 edges in $O(n\log^3 n)$ time and space and reports all k edges intersecting a query circle in $O(\log^3 n+k)$ worst-case time? The graph is embedded in the Euclidean plane: edges are nonzero closed line segments, distinct edge interiors are disjoint, and edges meet only at shared endpoints. A query supplies a center c and radius r > 0. Promise that the circle contains no graph vertex on its boundary and is tangent to no edge. Report each intersected input edge once. All hidden constants are independent of the graph, circle, and output size.

records.title: Does P equal NP?
records.formal: Does every language with polynomially bounded, polynomial-time verifiable certificates admit a deterministic polynomial-time decision algorithm? Equivalently, do there exist a deterministic Turing machine A and constants C,k such that, for every encoded Boolean formula F of bit length n, A decides whether F has a satisfying assignment and halts within $C(n+1)^k$ steps? The algorithm must give the correct answer on every input.

records.title: Do single-pair shortest paths require cubic-size min-plus circuits?
records.formal: For n >= 2, assign an arbitrary nonnegative real weight x_{ij} to every unordered edge {i,j} of the complete undirected graph on vertices 1,...,n. Define $f_n(x)=\min_{P:1\leadsto n}\sum_{e\in P}x_e$, where P ranges over simple paths. A circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with input gates x_{ij} and optional constants 0 and infinity, binary gates min(a,b) or a+b, unrestricted reuse of gate outputs, and one designated output. Its topology depends on n but not on x, and it must compute f_n exactly for every permitted weight assignment. Let s(n) be the minimum number of binary gates in such a circuit. Is s(n)=Omega(n^3)? Equivalently, do there exist constants c>0 and n0 such that every such circuit has at least c n^3 gates for every n>=n0?

records.title: Is weighted falsifiability of unambiguous DNFs in polynomial time?
records.formal: Is there a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in the total binary input length, that solves the following problem? The input consists of an unambiguous DNF $F=\bigvee_{j=1}^{m}T_j$ over n Boolean variables, nonnegative integer weights w_1,...,w_n encoded in binary, and an integer threshold t encoded in binary. Decide whether there exists $a\in\{0,1\}^n$ such that $F(a)=0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_i a_i\ge t$. Each T_j is an explicitly listed conjunction of literals. Unambiguous means that no assignment satisfies two distinct terms simultaneously.

records.title: Are splay trees dynamically optimal?
records.formal: Fix n ordered keys and an access sequence X. In the root-BST model, an access is served by rotations until its key is at the root; its cost is one plus the number of rotations. Let OPT(X) minimize total cost over offline executions, allowing an optimal initial tree. Is there a universal constant C such that, for every initial splay tree T₀ and every X, $\mathrm{cost}_{\mathrm{splay}}(X;T_0)\le C(\mathrm{OPT}(X)+n)$? The additive term allows an arbitrary initial configuration.

records.title: The online Boolean matrix–vector multiplication conjecture
records.formal: Given a Boolean matrix $M\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$, receive vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\{0,1\}^n$ one at a time. Output each Boolean product $(Mv_t)_i=\bigvee_{j=1}^{n}(M_{ij}\wedge(v_t)_j)$ before receiving $v_{t+1}$. Is there any constant $\varepsilon>0$ and randomized algorithm with total running time $O(n^{3-\varepsilon})$ and error probability at most $1/3$? The OMv conjecture asserts that there is no such algorithm. In this formulation the total includes preprocessing of $M$.

records.title: Do splay trees support deque operations in constant amortized time?
records.formal: Start from an arbitrary binary search tree containing $n$ ordered keys, and perform $m$ legal double-ended queue operations. Insert-min creates a new minimum as the root with the old tree as its right child; insert-max is symmetric. Delete-min splays the minimum to the root, removes it, and keeps its right subtree; delete-max is symmetric. Is the total number of primitive pointer operations and rotations always $O(n+m)$, with a universal constant? This is Tarjan’s deque conjecture for the specified splay implementation.

records.title: Can pointer-machine working-set heaps have constant amortized insertion and decrease-key?
records.formal: Does there exist a deterministic online priority queue in the pointer-machine model below and an absolute constant C such that every legal sequence of M operations, starting from an empty queue, has total cost at most $C(M+\sum_{x\ \mathrm{extracted}}\log \Gamma(x))$? The operations are insert, find-min, decrease-key, and extract-min. For an extracted item x, define $\Gamma(x)=1+$ the number of insertions strictly after x was inserted and before it was extracted, including inserted items that have already been removed. An insertion creates a distinct item and returns its handle; decrease-key receives that handle and its new key. Require exact answers for all sequences; melding is not required.

The input to each operation supplies the component’s root handle; identifying which component contains x is not a separate search problem.

records.title: Can reachability diameter be approximated within a constant in near-linear time?

records.title: Can an acyclic subgraph preserve a constant fraction of the optimal reachable pairs?
records.formal: For a finite directed graph G=(V,E), let $R(D)=|\{(u,v)\in V^2:u\ne v,\text{ a directed path from }u\text{ to }v\text{ exists in }D\}|$ and $\mathrm{OPT}(G)=\max\{R((V,F)):F\subseteq E,\ (V,F)\text{ is acyclic}\}$. Do there exist a constant alpha>0 and a deterministic algorithm running in time polynomial in |V|+|E| that, for every G, outputs F subset E with (V,F) acyclic and R((V,F)) >= alpha OPT(G)? records.title: Do pure pairing heaps support O(log log n) amortized decrease-key?
records.formal: For the pure pairing heap defined below, is there a universal constant C such that every legal sequence of M operations starting with empty heaps costs at most $C[M+D(1+\log N)+K(1+\log\log(N+2))]$? Here D counts delete-min operations, K counts decrease-key operations, and $N\ge2$ is the maximum of 2 and the total number of live items across all heaps at any moment. The allowed operations are make-heap, insert, find-min, meld, decrease-key, and delete-min. Count comparisons and pointer-machine steps; keys are distinct opaque values in a totally ordered set, compared at unit cost. Handles to the affected items and heaps are supplied.

records.title: Does the expected redundancy of optimal alphabetic trees with random weights converge?
records.formal: For each n >= 2, let $D=(D_1,\ldots,D_n)$ be uniform on the probability simplex, equivalently Dirichlet(1,...,1). Let $C_n(D)=\min_T\sum_{i=1}^n D_i d_T(i)$, where T ranges over full ordered binary trees with leaves 1,...,n in that left-to-right order and d_T(i) is the depth of leaf i, with root depth zero. Define $H(D)=-\sum_iD_i\log_2D_i$ and $r_n=\mathbb E_D[C_n(D)-H(D)]$. Does the real sequence r_n converge to a finite limit as n tends to infinity? This is a precise limit-existence target within the source’s broader request to determine the expected optimal cost.

records.title: Can four-sided skyline reporting match ordinary range reporting?
records.formal: Preprocess a static set $P\subseteq[N]^2$ of $N$ points, with distinct coordinates in each dimension, on a word RAM with $\Theta(\log N)$-bit words. Is there a structure using $N\log^{O(1)}N$ words that reports the skyline of $P\cap([a,b]\times[c,d])$ in worst-case $O(\log\log N+k)$ time, where $k$ is the number of reported points? A point is on the skyline if no other point in the query rectangle is at least as large in both coordinates and strictly larger in one.

records.title: Can lazy B-tree priority queues keep their I/O bounds with stable handles?
records.formal: Is there a deterministic comparison-based external-memory priority queue with a universal constant c of internal storage at most cB words that satisfies the following bounds for every capacity $N\ge B\ge2$? Starting empty and never holding more than N elements, it uses $O(1+N/B)$ external blocks, supports insertion and handle-based decrease-key in $O(1+\log_B\log_B N)$ worst-case I/Os, and supports extract-min in $O(1+B^{-1}\log_2 N+\log_B\log_B N)$ amortized I/Os. Every handle remains valid until its element is removed. All handle maintenance and lookup costs count. Each logarithm is truncated below at one.

records.title: Does worst-case Nearest Codeword hardness imply low-noise LPN hardness?
records.formal: Does the following implication hold? If binary Nearest Codeword is not in BPP, then no uniform probabilistic polynomial-time distinguisher D has advantage at least $n^{-c}$, for any fixed $c>0$ and all sufficiently large square n, between $(A,As+e)$ and $(A,u)$. Here $A\in\mathbb F_2^{n^2\times n}$, $s\in\mathbb F_2^n$, and $u\in\mathbb F_2^{n^2}$ are independent uniform random variables, and the coordinates of e are independent Bernoulli variables with rate $1/\sqrt n$. Advantage is the absolute difference of D’s acceptance probabilities in the two experiments.

records.title: Is perfect matching in general graphs in deterministic NC?
records.formal: Given a simple undirected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, can a deterministic parallel algorithm find a perfect matching, or report that none exists, in $(\log n)^{O(1)}$ time using $n^{O(1)}$ processors? A perfect matching is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges covering every vertex. Equivalently, seek a uniform polynomial-size, polylogarithmic-depth circuit family for the search problem. Graphs may contain odd cycles; no bipartition is supplied or promised.

records.title: How many rounds does triangle detection require in CONGEST?
records.formal: For arbitrary simple undirected n-vertex networks, determine the optimal worst-case randomized round complexity of triangle detection in CONGEST, up to constant factors. Each vertex initially knows its distinct O(log n)-bit identifier and its neighbors, and may send a separate O(log n)-bit message in each direction of every incident edge per synchronous round. On a triangle-free graph all vertices must output NO; otherwise at least one must output YES. The joint answer must be correct with probability at least 2/3 on every input and identifier assignment. The algorithm is uniform, has private random bits, and may know n. The currently established bounds are $\Omega(\log\log n)$ and $\widetilde O(n^{1/3})$.

records.title: Can a congested clique find a maximal independent set in constant rounds?
records.formal: Is there a randomized algorithm that, on every n-vertex simple input graph, finds a maximal independent set in O(1) rounds in the Congested Clique model, with success probability at least $1-n^{-c}$ for every requested fixed $c>0$? Processor v initially knows its identifier and incident input edges. Every ordered pair of processors may exchange an O(log n)-bit message per synchronous round, whether or not the input edge exists. Each processor outputs whether it belongs to an independent set that dominates every vertex outside it. The algorithm must be uniform across inputs; it cannot be chosen after seeing the graph.

records.title: Is the known exponent for distributed even-cycle detection optimal?
records.formal: For every fixed integer $k\ge3$, is $\widetilde\Omega(n^{1-1/k})$ a worst-case round lower bound for randomized detection of a simple cycle of length exactly 2k in the CONGEST model? The network is an arbitrary simple undirected n-vertex graph. Each vertex initially knows n, its distinct O(log n)-bit identifier, and its incident edges; each edge carries O(log n) bits per direction per synchronous round. If a cycle exists at least one vertex must output YES, and otherwise all must output NO. Require the joint answer to be correct with probability at least 2/3 on every input.

records.title: Does the specified weighted temporal logic express every weighted FO sentence over natural numbers?
records.formal: For every finite alphabet Sigma and every closed weighted first-order expression E in the fragment defined below, with weights in the semiring (N,+,times,0,1), does there exist a weighted temporal expression H in the specified grammar such that E(w)=H(w,1) for every nonempty finite word w over Sigma? The weighted temporal grammar is $H ::= 0\mid Ls\mid\langle s\rangle H\mid s\,U_w\,H\mid H+H\mid\operatorname{if}(\varphi,H,H)$, where s is a finite conditional expression returning a natural-number constant and phi is an ordinary Boolean LTL formula with both future and past. Its exact semantics and the source weighted-FO grammar are given in Model & notation. No additional weighted operator may be introduced. This fixes the natural-number instance of the weighted Kamp question discussed in Gastin’s December 2025 slides.

records.title: Can every fixed-dimensional Tarski problem be solved with O(log² n) queries?
records.formal: Let Q(n,k) be the minimum worst-case number of adaptive deterministic value queries needed to find any fixed point of an unknown monotone function $f:[n]^k\to[n]^k$, where [n]={1,...,n} and monotonicity is with respect to coordinatewise order. A query at x reveals the entire vector f(x). Is it true that for every integer k>=1 there is a constant C_k such that $Q(n,k)\le C_k(1+\log_2 n)^2$ for every n>=2? Arbitrary finite computation between queries is allowed. Constants may depend on k but not on n or f. This asks for an exponent independent of the fixed dimension, not a polynomial bound on C_k.

records.title: Does general rational linear programming have a strongly polynomial algorithm?
records.formal: Does there exist a deterministic algorithm, with fixed polynomials p and q, that solves every rational linear program $\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}$, where A has m rows and n columns, using at most p(m+n) elementary arithmetic, comparison, and data-transfer operations, while every intermediate rational number has binary encoding length at most q(N)? Here N is the total input bit length. Solving means returning an exact optimal rational solution if one exists, or correctly reporting infeasibility or an objective unbounded below.

records.title: Can randomness always be removed from polynomial-time decision algorithms?
records.formal: Does P=BPP? Precisely, for every language L for which a randomized Turing machine R runs in polynomial time on every input and every random tape, and satisfies $\Pr[R(x)=1_L(x)]\ge2/3$ for every binary string x, does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine deciding L correctly on every x? The polynomial time bound of the deterministic machine may depend on R.

Does it have an interactive proof with a $\operatorname{poly}(n)$-time verifier, a $\operatorname{poly}(T(n))$-time honest prover, and a constant completeness–soundness gap? Soundness must hold against arbitrarily powerful cheating provers. The target includes $T$ beyond the quasipolynomial range.

records.title: Higher-dimensional product expansion for structured Reed–Solomon codes
records.formal: For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, does there exist $\rho>0$ depending only on k and epsilon with the following property? Let q be prime, let $S_i\le\mathbb F_q^\times$ have pairwise coprime sizes $s_i$, and let $C_i=\{(f(a))_{a\in S_i}:\deg f<d_i\}$ with $1\le d_i<(1-\varepsilon)s_i$. Put $\Omega=\prod_i S_i$ and let $L_i$ be the arrays on Omega whose every i-axis line belongs to $C_i$. Every $M\in\sum_i L_i$ must admit a decomposition $M=\sum_i M_i$, $M_i\in L_i$, satisfying $|\operatorname{supp}M|\ge\rho\sum_i s_i\ell_i(M_i)$, where $\ell_i$ counts nonzero i-axis lines.

records.title: Is the matrix multiplication exponent equal to two?
records.formal: Fix the field of complex numbers. Let s(n) be the minimum number of arithmetic gates in a circuit that computes all entries of AB exactly for arbitrary n-by-n matrices A,B. Is it true that $\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists C_\varepsilon>0\;\forall n\ge2:\ s(n)\le C_\varepsilon n^{2+\varepsilon}$? Equivalently, is $\omega=\inf\{\tau:s(n)=O(n^\tau)\}=2$?

records.title: Does the smallest grammar problem admit a constant-factor approximation?
records.formal: Do there exist an absolute constant C and a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, for every explicit nonempty string s, outputs an acyclic context-free grammar generating exactly s whose size is at most $C g^*(s)$? There is one production per nonterminal, one designated start nonterminal, and every right-hand side is a nonempty string of terminals and nonterminals. The dependency graph on nonterminals must be acyclic. Grammar size is the sum of all right-hand-side lengths, and $g^*(s)$ is the minimum such size. The alphabet is part of the input, encoded by integer symbols in {1,...,|s|}.

records.title: Can LZ77 random access use linear compressed space and logarithmic query time?
records.formal: Given the greedy LZ77 parse with z phrases of a string $S[1..N]$ over an integer alphabet of size at most N, is there a deterministic word-RAM data structure using O(z) words in total that returns S[i] for any $1\le i\le N$ in worst-case O(log N) time? Words have $\Theta(\log N)$ bits. A phrase is a new literal or a longest prefix of the unparsed suffix having an occurrence starting earlier in S; overlapping copies are allowed. Space includes the stored parse and all query-support information. The uncompressed string is unavailable at query time.

records.title: Can pattern matching run in linear time in the LZ77 input size?
records.formal: Is there a deterministic algorithm that, given a valid LZ77 representation of z phrases of a text T of length N and an explicit nonempty pattern P of length m, decides whether P occurs contiguously in T in O(z+m) worst-case time? Self-referencing copy phrases are allowed. Symbols are integers in $\{1,\ldots,(z+m)^c\}$ for a fixed constant c. Use a word RAM with word size $\Theta(\log(N+m+2))$, the operations specified below, and O(z+m) working words. The input is the compressed text and the explicit pattern; all preprocessing is included.

records.title: Can a supplied Karp–Rabin fingerprint be verified in near-linear time?
records.formal: Given a string $S\in\{0,\ldots,\sigma-1\}^{n}$ and a prime $q$, with $\sigma,q\le n^{O(1)}$, define $h_q(x_1\cdots x_\ell)=\sum_{t=1}^{\ell}x_t\sigma^{\ell-t}\bmod q$. Can one decide in $O(n\log n)$ time whether there exist equal-length substrings $A,B$ of $S$ such that $A\ne B$ but $h_q(A)=h_q(B)$? The modulus is part of the input and cannot be replaced. The deterministic decision problem is the precise target here; the source also permits randomized certification that never accepts a colliding modulus and rejects a collision-free one only with small probability.

records.title: Can exact fully dynamic APSP have edge-linear amortized updates and polylogarithmic queries?
records.formal: For every fixed positive integer c, do there exist a deterministic data structure and constants a,d >= 1 such that the following holds for all n >= 2 and $n\le m\le n^2$? Maintain a directed simple graph on a fixed set of n vertices, with at most m edges at every time and integer edge weights in {1,...,n^c}, under single-edge insertions, deletions, and weight changes. Return the exact current distance from any queried vertex s to any queried vertex t in $O(\log^a n)$ worst-case time. After $O(n^d)$ preprocessing, require $O(m\log^a n)$ amortized time per update and polynomial space. Constants may depend on c, but not on n, m, the initial graph, or the operation sequence.

records.title: Is private PAC sample complexity polynomial in VC dimension and log-star Littlestone dimension?
records.formal: Is there a universal polynomial p such that every finite Boolean concept class C admits a realizable, possibly improper PAC learner using some number $m\le p(1+\mathrm{VC}(C),1+\log^*\mathrm{LD}(C))$ of independent labeled examples, with error at most 1/10 and confidence at least 9/10, while satisfying $(1,1/(100m^2))$-differential privacy? The learning guarantee must hold for every distribution on the domain and every target concept in C. Computation time is unrestricted. Take both dimensions to be at least one; constant classes can be handled separately.

records.title: Optimal private selection using only Gaussian queries
records.formal: For a finite set $Y$, public losses $\ell_y$ have sensitivity 1 under a one-record change in the database $X$. The only access to $X$ is through adaptive queries $q_i(X)+N(0,1/(2\rho_i))$, with sensitivity at most 1 and $\sum_i\rho_i\le\rho$. Can the algorithm output $\hat y$ satisfying $\mathbb E[\ell_{\hat y}(X)]-\min_y\ell_y(X)=O(\log|Y|/\sqrt\rho)$?

records.title: Optimal private selection using only Laplace queries
records.formal: Let $Y$ be a finite set of candidates, each with a public loss function $\ell_y$ of sensitivity one under a one-record database change. To access the database, an algorithm makes $k$ adaptive sensitivity-1 queries. Its answers are $q_i(X)+\mathrm{Lap}(k)$, where $k$ is the scale. Can it guarantee expected excess loss $O(\log|Y|)$ for arbitrary losses? The algorithm may choose the number of queries.

records.area: Database theory and finite model theory
records.title: Is containment of conjunctive queries under bag semantics decidable?
records.formal: Does a Turing machine exist that halts on every pair of finite conjunctive queries q_1 and q_2 with the same output arity and decides whether $q_1(D)(a)\le q_2(D)(a)$ for every finite bag database D over their common relational signature and every output tuple a? A query $q(x)\!:\!-A_1,\ldots,A_m$ is evaluated by $q(D)(a)=\sum_{h:h(x)=a}\prod_{j=1}^{m}D(A_j[h])$, where h ranges over assignments of its variables to the finite database domain and D(A_j[h]) is the nonnegative integer multiplicity of the instantiated tuple. Both input relations and query answers retain multiplicities.

records.area: Database theory and finite model theory
records.title: Does naive evaluation over p-stable semirings converge in O((p+1)n) rounds?
records.formal: Is there a universal constant C such that the following holds for every integer p>=0, every n>=1, every commutative p-stable semiring S, and every polynomial map F:S^n -> S^n with coefficients in S? Starting with x^(0)=(0,...,0), perform synchronous iteration x^(t+1)=F(x^(t)). There must exist an integer t<=C(p+1)n with x^(t+1)=x^(t). Here p-stability means $1\oplus a\oplus\cdots\oplus a^p=1\oplus a\oplus\cdots\oplus a^{p+1}$ for every a in S. The constant C is independent of the semiring, coefficients, number of monomials, and polynomial degrees. This is the grounded polynomial-system formulation of the source’s proposed linear convergence bound.

records.title: Erdős girth conjecture: is the classical spanner size bound tight?
records.formal: For every fixed integer $k\ge 2$, do there exist a constant $c_k>0$ and arbitrarily large simple undirected graphs $G$ with $n$ vertices, at least $c_k n^{1+1/k}$ edges, and no cycle of length at most $2k$? Equivalently, can the $O_k(n^{1+1/k})$ extremal upper bound for girth greater than $2k$ be attained up to a constant factor for every $k$? The first unsettled value is $k=4$: girth at least nine and $\Omega(n^{5/4})$ edges.

records.title: Does average-case NP hardness imply infinitely-often one-way functions?
records.formal: Does $\mathrm{DistNP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{HeurBPP}$ imply the existence of a polynomial-time computable function f with the following property? For every probabilistic polynomial-time inverter I and every constant c>0, infinitely many lengths n satisfy $\Pr[|z|=n\ \land\ f(z)=f(x)]<n^{-c}$, where $x\sim U(\{0,1\}^n)$ and $z\leftarrow I(1^n,f(x))$. The probability includes inverter randomness. This card fixes the infinitely-often security convention used by the cited characterization.
